key: And Jacob said unto Pharaoh: ‘The days of the years of my sojournings are a hundred and thirty years; few and evil have been the days of the years of my life, and they have not attained unto the days of the years of the life of my fathers in the days of their sojournings.’
s: Brought before Pharaoh by Joseph and asked his age, Jacob answers the king; Sforno, on 47:9, reads him as setting his years of sojourning apart from his years of life, which were few, since days passed in trouble are not called days of life.

evidence.gloss: As to your asking how many are the days of the years of my life, I say that the years of my life were few and evil, through much trouble over sustenance and the worries that befell me, for the days in which a man is in distress are not called days of the years of life; but the days of the years of my sojourning came in all to a hundred and thirty years.
